info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package social is posting to every social account you own, now or on a schedule.

get.summary: Returns the caller organization's connected and registered social channels, optionally filtered by provider (`?provider=x`) or employee/brand group (`?group=Antje%20Worring`).
get.description:
Returns the caller organization's connected and registered social channels,
optionally filtered by provider (`?provider=x`) or employee/brand group (`?group=Antje%20Worring`).

parameters.description: Provider keeps only channels on the named network (for example "x" or "linkedin"). Omit for all networks.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Group keeps only channels belonging to the named employee or brand group (matching groupId or case-insensitive groupName).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit bounds the maximum number of channels returned (default 200, max 1000).

get.summary: Returns the org's connected accounts — each one's id, network, handle, status and timestamps, most-recently-updated first.
get.description:
Returns the org's connected accounts — each one's id, network,
handle, status and timestamps, most-recently-updated first.

An account's provider access token is NEVER included in any response on this
surface. Only the publisher reads it.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description:
Provider keeps only accounts on one network — x, facebook, instagram,
linkedin, tiktok, youtube or threads. Omit it for every network. It is
lower-cased and trimmed before it is matched, and a value that names no
network simply matches nothing rather than being refused.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit bounds the page, defaulting to 200 and capped at 1000. It is a string
rather than an integer on purpose: the route parses it with a leading trim
and falls back to the default on anything it cannot read, so `?limit=%2050`
is a page of fifty today. An integer field would refuse the space and read
an unparseable value as zero, which is a different page.

delete.summary: Removes one connected account from the org and answers 204 with no body; an id that is not there is 404.
delete.description:
Removes one connected account from the org and answers 204 with no
body; an id that is not there is 404.

It removes the account record only. Posts that already published through it keep
their published state and their recorded external ids — this does not retract
anything from the network.

parameters.description: ID is the account or post to act on, taken from the path.

get.description:

put.summary: Replaces the account's network, handle and status with what the body carries, and answers with the stored row.
put.description:
Replaces the account's network, handle and status with what the
body carries, and answers with the stored row.

This is a REPLACEMENT, not a merge, which is the rule most easily got wrong: a
field the body omits is written as its default, so leaving out the handle blanks
it and leaving out the status resets it to connected. Send the whole record. The
same vocabularies as create apply, and an unknown network or status is refused
rather than coerced.

get.description: Lists the apps this org has sealed. The secret is not included.

put.description: Seals the apps in the body. A network left out is unchanged.

post.summary: Adapts ingestPostiz to a zip handler: it reads the bearer-free path token, decodes the body, and delegates.
post.description:
Adapts ingestPostiz to a zip handler: it reads the bearer-free
path token, decodes the body, and delegates. It runs outside Bridge auth because
the token IS the credential — no org, no bearer, nothing to validate upstream.

get.summary: Returns the org's posts — content, channel, status, scheduled time, media and timestamps — most-recently-updated first.
get.description:
Returns the org's posts — content, channel, status, scheduled time,
media and timestamps — most-recently-updated first.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Status keeps only posts in one state — draft, scheduled, published or
failed. Omit it for every state. The transient publishing claim is not a
user-visible state and matching it is not useful.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
Limit bounds the page, defaulting to 200 and capped at 1000. A string for
the same reason accountFilter.Limit is.

post.summary: Stores a post for the org and answers 201 with the stored row.
post.description:
Stores a post for the org and answers 201 with the stored row.

A post created as scheduled for a time that has already passed is published
IMMEDIATELY, and the row returned carries that outcome — this is the one behaviour
a reader would otherwise miss. A future-scheduled post is left for the scheduler,
and a draft is left alone. Publishing never fails the creation: the post is stored
either way, and a publish that could not run leaves the row for the scheduler to
retry.

delete.summary: Removes one post from the org and answers 204 with no body; an id that is not there is 404.
delete.description:
Removes one post from the org and answers 204 with no body; an id that
is not there is 404.

It deletes the record here only. A post that has already published is not
retracted from the network by deleting it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the account or post to act on, taken from the path.

get.summary: Returns one of the org's posts by id, with its current status, scheduled time, media and — once it has published — the account and external id it published under.
get.description:
Returns one of the org's posts by id, with its current status, scheduled
time, media and — once it has published — the account and external id it published
under. 404 when there is no such post for this org.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the account or post to act on, taken from the path.

put.summary: Replaces the post's content, channel, status, scheduled time and media with what the body carries, and answers with the stored row.
put.description:
Replaces the post's content, channel, status, scheduled time and media
with what the body carries, and answers with the stored row.

A REPLACEMENT, not a merge: an omitted field is written as its default, so
omitting media clears it and omitting the status resets the post to draft.
`content` is required on every update. Unlike create, this never triggers a
publish — moving a post's scheduled time into the past here leaves it for the
scheduler; publish now is its own operation.

post.summary: Publishes the post immediately to the connected accounts on its channel and answers with the updated row, carrying the account and external id it published under.
post.description:
Publishes the post immediately to the connected accounts on its channel
and answers with the updated row, carrying the account and external id it
published under.

It is IDEMPOTENT: a post that has already published, or that another caller is
publishing right now, comes back unchanged rather than being posted twice. That
claim is taken before any network call, which is what makes a double submit safe.

The two failure shapes differ on purpose. Having no connected account for the
channel is the caller's to fix, so it is recorded ON the post as failed with the
reason and answers normally. A deployment that lacks the network's own credentials
cannot publish for anyone, so that is a 503 naming exactly what is missing.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the account or post to act on, taken from the path.

get.summary: Reports each supported network's publish-readiness: whether this deployment holds the OAuth application credentials for it and, when it does not, exactly which environment variables are missing.
get.description:
Reports each supported network's publish-readiness: whether this
deployment holds the OAuth application credentials for it and, when it does not,
exactly which environment variables are missing.

This is a live read of the deployment's own configuration, not a static list of
networks — it answers "can I connect this today", which is what a connect
affordance and a pre-cutover checklist both need. It says nothing about whether
the caller has connected an account; that is the accounts listing.

get.summary: Returns four counts for the caller's org: total posts, how many are scheduled, how many have published, and how many accounts are connected.
get.description:
Returns four counts for the caller's org: total posts, how many are
scheduled, how many have published, and how many accounts are connected. It is
the dashboard roll-up, computed over the org's own rows in one read.

releaseUrl.description: ReleaseURL is the public permalink of the published post on the social network when known.

scheduleAt.description: ScheduleAt is the scheduled publish time in unix seconds (0 when unscheduled or immediate).

status.description: Status is the post lifecycle state: draft, scheduled, published, failed, or mirrored.

updatedAt.description: UpdatedAt is when the post was last updated, in unix seconds.

data.description: Data holds the matching posts ordered newest-updated first.

accountId.description: AccountID optionally pins the post to a specific connected channel ID.

channel.description: Channel is the target social network identifier (defaults to "x").

content.description: Content is the updated post body text (required).

media.description: Media replaces the attached media URL list.

scheduleAt.description: ScheduleAt is the scheduled unix timestamp in seconds.

status.description: Status is the post lifecycle state (draft, scheduled, published, or failed; defaults to draft).

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the account was connected, as a unix timestamp in seconds.

disabled.description:
Disabled is true when posting to this channel has been paused without
disconnecting its stored credentials.

externalId.description:
ExternalID is the platform id the sealed token is stored under. Empty for
an account recorded by hand, before a consent named one. A publish uses
it to choose that token rather than another account on the same network.

groupId.description:
GroupID is the deterministic identifier of the employee or brand channel
group this channel is organized under. Optional.

groupName.description:
GroupName is the employee or brand group label (for example "Antje Worring",
"Zach Kelling", or "Hanzo AI") used to organize and fan out posts across a
person's or team's channels. Optional.

handle.description:
Handle is the account's public name on the network, as the customer knows
it. Trimmed and bounded at 1024 characters.

Example: "@acme"

id.description:
ID is the account's identifier, minted on connect and the id every later
call addresses it by.

Example: "acct_7f3c1a"

name.description:
Name is the channel's human-readable display name on the network (for
example "Antje Worring" or "Hanzo AI"). Optional.

picture.description:
Picture is the avatar URL of the connected channel profile, when reported
by the network. Optional.

profile.description:
Profile is the canonical profile identifier or URL slug on the network.
Optional.

provider.description:
Provider is the network this account is on: x, facebook, instagram,
linkedin, tiktok, youtube or threads.

Example: "x"

refreshNeeded.description:
RefreshNeeded is true when the upstream OAuth token has expired or requires
interactive reconnection before publishing.

status.description:
Status is the connection lifecycle: connected, disconnected or error. Only
a connected account is a publish target.

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt is when the account row last changed, as a unix timestamp in
seconds. The listing is ordered by it, newest first.

handle.description:
Handle is the account's public name on the network, as the customer knows it
(`@acme`). Trimmed and bounded at 1024 characters.

Example: "@acme"

provider.description:
Provider is the network this account is on: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin,
tiktok, youtube or threads. Omitted means x. Anything else is refused rather
than coerced, because a stored account on a network that does not exist can
never be published through.

Example: "x"

status.description:
Status is the connection lifecycle: connected, disconnected or error.
Omitted means connected. Only a connected account is a publish target.

handle.description:
Handle is the account's public name on the network. Omitting it BLANKS the
stored handle: this is a replacement, not a merge.

Example: "@acme"

provider.description:
Provider is the network this account is on: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin,
tiktok, youtube or threads. Omitted means x.

Example: "x"

status.description:
Status is the connection lifecycle: connected, disconnected or error.
Omitting it RESETS the account to connected.

data.description: Data is the accounts, most-recently-updated first, bounded by the limit.

accountId.description:
AccountID / ExternalID / Error are server-managed publish results, set only by
the publish path (never by a client update): the account a post was published
through, the provider's returned external post id (for reconciliation), and the
last failure reason. Empty until a publish attempt lands.
AccountID is the connected account the post went out through. Absent until
a publish succeeds.

channel.description:
Channel is the network this post targets: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin,
tiktok, youtube or threads. It is the channel whose CONNECTED accounts a
publish fans out to.

Example: "x"

content.description:
Content is the post's text, bounded at 8192 characters.

Example: "Shipping today."

createdAt.description: CreatedAt is when the post was created, as a unix timestamp in seconds.

error.description:
Error is why the last publish attempt failed, verbatim and bounded. Absent
when no attempt has failed; cleared by a later success. A post published to
several accounts that only some took is published, and this names the rest.

externalGroup.description: ExternalGroup is the Postiz group the post belongs to (optional).

externalId.description:
ExternalID is the id the network returned for the published post, which is
what reconciles this row against the post on the network. Absent until a
publish succeeds.

externalIdPostiz.description: ExternalIDPostiz is the Postiz post id, set only for origin=postiz rows.

externalIntegrationId.description: ExternalIntegrationId is the Postiz integration id that published it.

id.description:
ID is the post's identifier, minted on create and the id every later call
addresses it by.

Example: "post_91ab20"

media.description:
Media is the post's attached media as a list of URLs (images today; the
composer's URL field now, an S3 picker later, populate it). Stored as a JSON
array in the media TEXT column and ALWAYS serialized as an array (never null),
so a client can rely on `media` being present. Bounded at the write layer
(normMedia in social.go): each URL clipped to maxField, the list to maxMedia.

origin.description:
Origin is who owns the post: "native" (a Hanzo user created it) or
"postiz" (mirrored from Postiz via ingest/poller). Mirrored posts are
read-only — clients may not create, update, publish or schedule them.

releaseUrl.description: ReleaseURL is the live URL Postiz returned for the published post.

scheduleAt.description:
ScheduleAt is when the post is due, as a unix timestamp in SECONDS. 0 means
unscheduled. It is meaningful only while the status is scheduled — a
scheduled post whose time has arrived is published by the scheduler.

status.description:
Status is the post's lifecycle state: draft, scheduled, published or failed.
A fifth, transient publishing state exists while a publish attempt holds the
claim; it is never settable from a request and a caller sees it only if it
reads a post mid-attempt.

updatedAt.description:
UpdatedAt is when the post row last changed, as a unix timestamp in seconds.
The listing is ordered by it, newest first.

channel.description:
Channel is the network to publish to: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin,
tiktok, youtube or threads. Omitted means x.

Example: "x"

content.description:
Content is the post's text. Required — an empty body is a 400 — and bounded
at 8192 characters, comfortably above every network's own limit.

Example: "Shipping today."

media.description:
Media is the post's attached media as URLs, at most 10, each bounded at 1024
characters. Blank entries are dropped. Omitting it CLEARS any stored media.

scheduleAt.description:
ScheduleAt is when to publish, as a unix timestamp in SECONDS. 0 means
unscheduled. A negative value is clamped to 0. It only matters for a post
whose status is scheduled.

status.description:
Status is the post's lifecycle state: draft, scheduled, published or failed.
Omitted means draft. The transient publishing claim is never settable here —
accepting it from a request would let a caller wedge or replay the guard that
stops two publishers double-posting the same row.

channel.description:
Channel is the network to publish to: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin,
tiktok, youtube or threads. Omitted means x.

Example: "x"

content.description:
Content is the post's text. Required on every update, and bounded at 8192
characters.

Example: "Shipping today."

media.description:
Media is the post's attached media as URLs, at most 10. Omitting it CLEARS
any stored media: this is a replacement, not a merge.

scheduleAt.description:
ScheduleAt is when to publish, as a unix timestamp in SECONDS. 0 means
unscheduled. Moving it into the past here does NOT publish the post — that is
the scheduler's to notice, or the publish operation's.

status.description:
Status is the post's lifecycle state: draft, scheduled, published or failed.
Omitting it RESETS the post to draft.

data.description: Data is the posts, most-recently-updated first, bounded by the limit.

credentialsConfigured.description:
CredentialsConfigured is whether this deployment holds every OAuth
application credential the network needs. It is a statement about the
DEPLOYMENT, not about the caller: a connected account also needs its own
access token before a post can go out.

missingCredentials.description:
MissingCredentials names the environment variables still unset for this
network, so the answer is an installation instruction rather than a refusal.
Absent when the credentials are complete. Only the NAMES appear here; a
credential value is never reported.

provider.description:
Provider is the network: x, facebook, instagram, linkedin, tiktok, youtube
or threads.

Example: "x"

data.description:
Data is one row per supported network, in the product's fixed order: x,
facebook, instagram, linkedin, tiktok, youtube, threads.

accounts.description: Accounts is how many accounts the org has connected, in any status.

posts.description: Posts is how many posts the org has, in any state.

published.description: Published is how many of them have published.

scheduled.description: Scheduled is how many of them are waiting for their scheduled time.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
